title: 2026-06-03-spectral-search-retrofit-pilot-scouting
summary: Initial discovery for retrofitting Orion's product search to a vector-first rerank pipeline. Discussed embedding dimensionality, vector DB integration patterns (fan-out vs hybrid), hosting options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC), throughput targets, SLOs, and security/compliance needs. Agreed to run a small benchmark and exchange a security questionnaire.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-03
Start: 16:30 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Orion Eng Lead), Marta (Orion PM), Samir (Orion Security)

Summary (auto): Discuss retrofit path for adding embeddings + rerank to existing inverted-index product search. Considerations: latency budget 120ms p95 for product page queries; throughput target 700 qps spiky; plans for canonical canonicalization of product metadata, embedding reindex cadence.

00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): Okay everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Alex on the Redwood side and Priya is our systems SE, she'll jump into infra and perf details. Jordan, Marta, Samir — thanks for taking the time. Can you give a quick overview of the current search stack?
00:20 Jordan (Orion Eng Lead): Yeah hi quick background: we run Elasticsearch for product search, with some bespoke ranking rules. Traffic is mainly US with EU slow but growing, product catalog is about 12M SKUs, 1200 writes per minute, reindex nightly. Queries are around 700 qps peak, taily at 1.2k for holiday spikes. We're looking to add a semantic rerank after our exact-match recall.
00:50 Marta (Orion PM): The goals are simple: relevancy lift for long-tail queries, and maintain 120ms p95 on product page search, ideally cost-neutral.
01:10 Priya (Redwood SE): Nice. So two common patterns: 1) hybrid pipeline — run inverted index to get candidates then embed+rerank, or 2) embed-first fanout — embed query then nearest-neighbor to fetch candidates from vector DB, then optional rerank. For you given catalog size and strong term signals, hybrid is typical.
01:40 Jordan: Yeah we like hybrid cause term matches are crucial. What's the perf overhead for doing rerank in-line?
02:00 Priya: It depends on embedding dims and model. For a 1536-d embedding using a 16-bit quantized model, per-query encode ~6-12ms on GPU if batched, but at low-latency needs it's often CPU-based or small GPU pools. The heavy part is the ANN search (vector DB) and then model-based re-score. With Redwood we can push rerank to a hosted dedicated pool or run in your VPC/private deployment.
02:35 Samir (Orion Security): Quick security callout — we need SOC 2, isolation for PII, envelope encryption with our KMS, and audit logs for every inference call. Are those supported?
02:50 Alex: Yes, we support SOC2 customers and have Private deployments that integrate with customer KMS/HSM and produce audit trails. We'll share our security pack. Priya can add details.
03:05 Priya: For Dedicated you get network isolation and reserved capacity; Private (VPC) gives you full control over KMS and private egress. For audit logs, our Console can export request/response metadata without storing PII fields, we also do configurable redaction.
03:30 Marta: Good. On the catalog side: we have dense attributes, we also add product embeddings daily. Curious about embedding dimensionality — we've seen 768 vs 1536 vs 2048 recommendations. Tradeoffs?
04:00 Priya: Higher dims usually improve representational capacity, but increase index size and ANN latency. For rerank it's common to use 768 or 1024 for balance. If you plan to store all product vectors in VDB, 12M * 1024 floats ~ 49GB in float32 — with quantization and IVF/HNSW compression it's much smaller. We typically recommend 768 for throughput-first, 1024 for higher fidelity.
04:40 Jordan: Do you provide embedding model recommendations? We currently use an in-house small model for embeddings and results vary.
04:55 Alex: Redwood has a model catalog — we can suggest a few open models we've verified across latency and quality. We can share runbooks for A/Bing the embeddings. Also can host your model if you require.
05:15 Jordan: Hosting our model privately would be interesting, we do have IP concerns.
05:25 Samir: Yes, for regulated suppliers we need private model hosting behind our VPC and no logs leaving the environment.
05:35 Priya: Private deployment supports that; we can deploy the inference runtime in your VPC or on-prem. It integrates with your KMS and logs stay on the network. Note though the ops bar is higher for private infra.
05:55 Marta: Ok ops question — how do we handle cache and KV state for seq-gen or rerank KV cache?
06:10 Priya: We do prefix caching and KV cache for decoder models, but for rerank typically stateless encode + ANN + scorer. Caching is useful for high QPS common queries — Redwood Console shows token-level breakdown to tune caching policies.
06:35 Jordan: On vector DB integration, we've looked at Pinecone and OpenSearch vectors internally. What's the pattern with Redwood? Do you ship to an external VDB or host the index inside Redwood?
06:50 Priya: Redwood integrates both ways: 1) we can call out to your vector DB (e.g., Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, OpenSearch) for nearest neighbor retrieval, or 2) we can host a co-located ANN layer in the Dedicated offering. Many customers prefer running the VDB themselves for control, but some prefer Redwood-managed for simplicity.
07:15 Jordan: Latency-wise, if we call out to an external VDB over the network, what's the tail impact?
07:30 Priya: Network adds variance; we aim to keep end-to-end under your p95 budget via routing and caching. For strict SLOs, Dedicated with co-located ANN or Private with local VDB often yields the best tail latency.
07:50 Marta: Cost question: is it cheaper to run the rerank model on CPU with quantized weights or go GPU?
08:05 Priya: Cost/latency tradeoff — quantized CPU can be good for lower throughput, but at 700 qps spike you'll likely want GPU pooling or many CPU cores. For tight p95 it's common to use GPUs (A10/A100) with batching. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching params per workload.
08:30 Jordan: Quick ask — can Redwood do partial rerank (only rerank top 20 candidates) to reduce model calls?
08:40 Priya: Absolutely. Typical flow: retrieve 50-200 term candidates, embed+ANN narrow, then rerank top 20-50. That reduces token and model cost significantly while preserving relevance.
09:05 Alex: I'm going to pivot to next steps and benchmarks — Jordan, what would you like us to run to validate?
09:15 Jordan: Ideally a smoke benchmark that mimics our traffic: 700 qps peak, mix of short product page queries (80%) and exploratory queries (20%). Also measure p95 end-to-end and cost per 10k queries.
09:35 Priya: We can run a 1k query-per-second bench for a 15-minute window against a sample shard of your catalog (we usually recommend 1-2M items for bench). We'll replicate your hybrid pipeline and quantify cost & p95. For Dedicated we can test on a 2-node pool first.
09:55 Samir: Security benchmark — we'll want to run a compliance checklist and share a redacted sample audit trail.
10:05 Alex: We'll send the security pack and a data flow diagram template.
10:15 Marta: Who owns the integration work? Our infra team or Redwood professional services?
10:25 Alex: Many customers do a joint approach: Redwood SE supports design and initial pilot; your infra executes VPC/DNS and we provide IaC snippets and runbooks. If you want hand-holding, PS can do it.
10:40 Jordan: Licensing and pricing? We have to compare hosted variable cost vs Dedicated monthly commit — which is better for us?
10:55 Priya: Hosted is lowest friction; you pay per token/embedding and Redwood does autoscaling. Dedicated gives predictable cost with reserved GPU capacity and lower per-unit cost at scale; Private adds a platform fee and support. Given your steady 700 qps with spikes, Dedicated with burst could be cost efficient. We'll model that with your query mix.
11:20 Jordan: Any competitor concerns? We've looked at Anthropic/Claude, OpenAI, and standalone vector vendors.
11:35 Alex: We often see customers use vector DB + separate model hosting; Redwood offers the unified runtime and tooling to reduce integration drift. We also have fallbacks to cheaper models for graceful degradation.
11:50 Marta: Ok let's talk timeline — if we decide to pilot, when can we start?
12:00 Priya: We can do a 4-week pilot: week 1 scoping + data prep, week 2 bench + integration, week 3 live pilot on a small traffic slice, week 4 analysis and recommendations.
12:20 Jordan: That'd work. We have a holiday blackout in late June but could start mid-July.
12:30 Samir: One more — data residency, our EU customers require data to stay in EU region. How does Redwood handle region routing?
12:45 Priya: We support region routing for Hosted and can place Dedicated/Private in EU clouds; Private gives the most control since you manage the infra. We'll note that in the security document.
13:05 Alex: Quick recap and actions.
13:10 Alex: (summarizes) Redwood to send security pack, throughput worksheet, and model recommendations. Redwood SE to run bench on sample shard once Orion provides sample data and expected query mix. Orion to provide compliance contact and sample query logs. Schedule pilot kickoff mid-July if agreed.
13:40 Marta: Sounds good. Also can you share a short doc on embedding dim tradeoffs and a cost model for 768 vs 1024?
13:55 Priya: Yep — we have one-page guidance and a cost sheet, will share.
14:10 Jordan: Thanks all, that was helpful.
14:20 Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with next steps.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hears ("K-V cash" for KV cache), product names sometimes misspelled (Consolee), filler words kept.
